name: Hungary: Budapest, Eger, Pécs and Lake Balaton

cities.base: District VII, the old Jewish Quarter: Dohány Synagogue and Szimpla on the doorstep, a walk to Andrássy út and the river. Kayak's weekday average was 183 dollars, November 92.
cities.name: Budapest

cities.base: The old town round Dobó tér, under the castle: everything is a walk, and the wine valley is walkable. November averages 70 dollars, 3-stars from 47.
cities.name: Eger

cities.base: Inside the old town near the cathedral, so the museums, Király utca and dinner are on foot. Hotel prices were not found.
cities.name: Pécs

cities.base: Balatonfüred, on the north shore by the station and the lakefront: Tihany is 9 km away and Keszthely a 53 km day. Hotel prices were not found.
cities.name: Lake Balaton (Balatonfüred and Tihany)

places.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
places.note: The Danube-front parliament, seen inside only on a 45 minute audio-guide tour; non-EU adults pay 23,150 forints (about 72 dollars), EU citizens 14,270. Book online 1 to 3 weeks ahead (2+ in July and August), bring photo ID, allow 15 minutes for security.

places.name: Fisherman's Bastion
places.note: Frigyes Schulek's seven-turreted lookout terrace, built 1895 to 1902, with the best view of Parliament across the river. The lower terraces are free and open round the clock; the upper walls charge a small fee in the daytime and are free in the evening, so come at dusk.

places.name: Matthias Church
places.note: The Gothic church beside Fisherman's Bastion; pair the two in one Castle Hill morning. Hours and ticket price were not confirmed, so check the price and hours before you go.

places.name: Buda Castle
places.note: Béla IV built the first palace here in 1247 to 1265; what you see is the Baroque palace of 1749 to 1769, rebuilt after the Second World War. The courtyards and terraces are free to walk; the National Gallery is inside, so give the hill a whole morning.

places.name: Hungarian National Gallery
places.note: Hungarian art from medieval altarpieces and Gothic panels through to the 20th century, in the castle palace. Hours, closing day (often Monday) and ticket price were not confirmed: check the price and hours before you plan around it.

places.name: Hungarian National Museum
places.note: Founded in 1802, in Mihály Pollack's neoclassical building of 1837 to 1847, the national history collection. Hours and ticket price unknown, so check the price before going.

places.name: House of Terror
places.note: The building that served as headquarters first for the Arrow Cross and then the ÁVH secret police, now a museum of both regimes; the basement cells are the part people remember. Hours and ticket price unknown, so check the price and hours.

places.name: Dohány Street Synagogue
places.note: Ludwig Förster's synagogue, built 1854 to 1859, 75m long and 43.6m high, the centre of the Jewish Quarter. Hours and ticket price were not confirmed; check the price and hours before you go.

places.name: St Stephen's Basilica
places.note: Begun in 1851; the dome collapsed in 1858 and had to be rebuilt, which is why it took decades. Hours and ticket price unknown, so check the price before going.

places.name: Gellért Hill Citadella
places.note: The fortress the Austrians built with forced labour after 1848 and finished in 1854. It reopened on 5 April 2026 after years of renovation; the hilltop view is free, but confirm before you climb, and check the price of any exhibition inside.

places.name: Széchenyi Chain Bridge
places.note: Opened in 1849 to a design by William Tierney Clark, the bridge that joins Pest to the foot of Castle Hill. Free and always open: walk it after dark.

places.name: Heroes' Square
places.note: The Millennium Monument, inaugurated in 1906, at the top of Andrássy út. Free at any hour; do it on the way to the Széchenyi Baths in City Park.

places.name: Hungarian State Opera House
places.note: Miklós Ybl's opera house, opened in 1884, halfway up Andrássy út. Tour times and ticket prices were not confirmed, so check the price and the season's programme before building an evening round it.

places.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
places.note: Győző Czigler's neo-baroque bath of 1913; this is the bath to do, since Gellért is closed until 2028. A day ticket with locker is 13,200 forints (about 41 dollars) Monday to Thursday and 14,800 (about 46) Friday to Sunday, a cabin 1,000 more. Weekends open at 08:00, Fridays run to 22:00.

places.name: Central Market Hall
places.note: Samu Pecz's iron market hall, opened in February 1897 and restored 1991 to 1997, with food stalls upstairs. Free to enter; Saturdays close by 15:00, and the sources disagree about Sunday (one lists 10:00 to 16:00, one says shut), so don't count on it.

places.name: Memento Park
places.note: 42 communist-era statues moved out of the city's squares and set up here in 1993. About 10 dollars on the official ticket; it is 10 km out, so pair it with nothing else that afternoon.

places.name: N28 Wine and Kitchen
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand wine bistro: soup, main and dessert from the summer menu came to 17,890 forints plus 15% service, about 64 dollars, before wine. Closed Sunday and Monday; book for dinner.

places.name: Cabrio
places.note: Bib Gourmand with a menu that changes regularly; a sample starter, main and dessert came to 10,700 forints plus 15% service, about 38 dollars. Dinner only Wednesday to Friday from 17:00, lunch too on Saturday and Sunday (Sunday ends 18:00); closed Monday and Tuesday.

places.name: Goli
places.note: Middle Eastern Bib Gourmand: order the lemon chicken shawarma and the knafeh, about 33 dollars with an espresso on the brunch menu. Dinner nightly from 17:00; brunch runs 10:30 to 16:00 at weekends (the site says Friday to Sunday in one place, Friday and Saturday in another).

places.name: Retro Lángos
places.note: Fried dough done right, 4.6 from over 20,000 Google reviews: lángos with sour cream and cheese is 3,490 forints, about 11 dollars. The tourist lángos bars on Duna utca charge 4,990 to 5,490 plus 15% service for the same thing.

places.name: Szimpla Kert
places.note: The original ruin bar, opened 2002, holding 580 in a gutted tenement; free entry, a half-litre draft 2,200 to 2,500 forints, pálinka 3,000. Queues on Friday and Saturday nights, it closes at 04:00, and the Sunday 09:00 to 14:00 producers' market is the daytime way in.

places.name: Eger Castle
places.note: Rebuilt after the Mongols in 1241, it held out through the 1552 siege; it fell in 1596, and the Austrians blew up half the outer fort in 1701. The ticket is 4,800 forints (about 15 dollars), 2,400 in the evening; exhibitions 09:00 to 18:00, the casemates from 10:00, the grounds gate 06:00 to 22:00.

places.name: Eger Basilica
places.note: The neoclassical cathedral of 1836, 4.8 on Google; free to walk in outside services. The tower is 1,500 forints, the crypt 500 and a guided visit 1,500, about 5, 2 and 5 dollars.

places.name: Kethüda Minaret
places.note: A 17th-century Ottoman minaret, among the northernmost left standing in Europe. 1,000 forints, about 3 dollars, cash only; autumn hours to 2 November are 10:00 to 16:45.

places.name: Lyceum Astronomical Museum and Camera Obscura
places.note: Miksa Hell installed the camera obscura in 1779, and the tower top gives the best view of the town. Hours and ticket price were not confirmed, so check the price and the demonstration times.

places.name: Archiepiscopal Palace Visitor Centre
places.note: The 18th-century Baroque residence of Eger's archbishops, next to the Basilica. Closed Mondays; check the price, it was not confirmed.

places.name: City Under the City
places.note: The cellar network Bishop Fenessy had dug in the late 1600s, under the old town, seen on a 45 to 50 minute guided tour for about 14 dollars. Last tours go earlier on weekdays: 10:00 to 16:00 Sunday to Thursday, to 17:30 Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Valley of the Beautiful Women
places.note: The valley of wine cellars on the edge of town, 4.7 from 22,774 Google reviews; free to wander, you pay per tasting. Many cellars shut on Mondays; flights run from 1,990 forints at cellar 46 to 3,490 to 6,990 at Juhász, cellar 38.

places.name: Dobó István Square
places.note: The main square, named for István Dobó, who commanded the 1552 defence, under the castle hill. Free, always open; it is where you cross the town ten times, best in the evening when the castle is lit.

places.name: Turkish Bath
places.note: The only Ottoman bathhouse surviving from the early 17th century; a 2.5 hour ticket is 4,600 forints, about 14 dollars. Opening varies: 16:30 Monday and Tuesday, 15:00 Wednesday and Thursday, 13:00 Friday, 09:00 weekends, always to 21:00.

places.name: Retro Múzeum Eger
places.note: Everyday objects from the socialist decades, 4.9 on Google from 451 reviews; about 13 dollars. Open daily 10:00 to 18:00, which makes it the Monday answer when the castle museums close.

places.name: Géza Gárdonyi Memorial Museum
places.note: A small memorial museum to the writer Géza Gárdonyi in the castle's Bebek bastion; add it to the castle visit. About 5 dollars; closed Mondays.

places.name: HBH Sörház és Étterem
places.note: Beer-house restaurant near Dobó tér, 4.5 from 4,122 Google reviews: soup, main and dessert came to 9,100 forints, about 28 dollars, with no service charge stated. Open daily, to 23:00 on Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Főtér Cafe Restaurant
places.note: On the main square, for lunch with the castle in view: soup, main and dessert came to 9,070 forints, about 31 dollars once the 10% service charge goes on. Open daily 10:00 to 22:00.

places.name: Kulacs Csárda
places.note: The csárda in the cellar valley: a soup, the pork knuckle and a dessert came to 9,500 forints plus 12% service, about 33 dollars, with house wine at 800 forints a decilitre. Closes 20:30 except Friday and Saturday (22:00).

places.name: Mamma Mia Pizza e Pasta
places.note: The cheap night in: a Margherita, a dessert and a beer come to 5,840 forints, about 18 dollars; pizzas run 3,100 to 4,800, pasta 3,600 to 5,300. Closed Mondays and, per the site, 5 to 11 September.

places.name: Szépasszonyvölgy Cellar 46 (Tóth Ferenc)
places.note: A family cellar in the valley: three wines for 1,990 forints, about 6 dollars, or five for 5,500; reviewers find it dearer than its neighbours. Closed Tuesdays; opens 10:00 Saturday to Monday, 12:00 Friday, 13:00 Wednesday and Thursday.

places.name: Butykos Kisvendéglő
places.note: A cellar-restaurant in the valley that works as a wine stop: three 1dl glasses of Eger wine at 950 forints each, about 9 dollars, bottles 5,400 to 7,800. Closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Bolyki Pincészet
places.note: A winery on the edge of town, 4.7 on Google; the tour and tasting is about 20 dollars, a longer cellar journey 34. Sundays close at 15:00, Saturdays run to 22:00.

places.name: Early Christian Necropolis (Cella Septichora)
places.note: The 4th-century painted Roman burial chambers under the cathedral square, UNESCO-listed since 2000; the World Heritage ticket is about 12 dollars and is valid two days. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Pécs Cathedral
places.note: Basilica of St Peter and St Paul: Roman-era foundations, a Romanesque rebuild after the 1064 fire, and the four-towered neo-Romanesque shell Friedrich von Schmidt gave it in 1882 to 1891. About 12 dollars; Sunday opens 11:30.

places.name: Mosque of Pasha Qasim
places.note: A 16th-century Ottoman mosque, now the Catholic Candlemas church, with the mihrab still in the wall and the Christian altar beside it. Hours and price unknown; check the price, and avoid Mass times.

places.name: Zsolnay Cultural Quarter
places.note: The 19th-century Zsolnay ceramics factory turned into museums, workshops and galleries, 2 km east of the old town. The one-day ticket to all the exhibitions is about 32 dollars; hours were not confirmed, so check before going.

places.name: Csontváry Museum
places.note: The museum of the painter Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka, next to the cathedral quarter; about 10 dollars. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Zsolnay Porcelain Museum
places.note: The Zsolnay family's ceramics, in a building dating to 1324; about 10 dollars. Closed Mondays; do it the same morning as Vasarely next door.

places.name: Victor Vasarely Museum
places.note: The largest collection of Victor Vasarely's op art anywhere; about 10 dollars. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Barbican
places.note: The round gate tower of the 1400s town walls, put up against the Ottomans. Hours and any entry price were not confirmed; seen from outside, it is free, so check the price only if you want inside.

places.name: Pécs Synagogue
places.note: The 1869 synagogue in Neoclassical and Moorish Revival style. Hours and price unknown, so check the price and opening before you walk over.

places.name: Pécs TV Tower
places.note: A 197m tower from 1973 on the 535m Misina hill above town, with the view from the top; about 5 dollars. Open to 19:00 Monday to Thursday, 20:00 Friday and Saturday, 18:00 Sunday.

places.name: Zsolnay Mausoleum
places.note: The Zsolnay family burial chamber, lined in eosin-glazed porcelain; about 8 dollars. Closed Mondays; add it to the Zsolnay Quarter afternoon.

places.name: Tettye Ruins
places.note: The ruins on the Tettye hillside above the old town, a short climb from Tettye Vendéglő. Price and hours were not confirmed; check the price, and combine it with dinner up there.

places.name: Kodály Center
places.note: The 2010 concert hall, with guided tours of the building. Hours and ticket prices unknown; check the price and the concert listings.

places.name: Tettye Vendéglő
places.note: The Hungarian restaurant up on the Tettye slope, 4.6 from 3,125 Google reviews: soup, main and dessert came to 9,200 forints, about 29 dollars. Closed Monday, and Sunday ends at 18:00.

places.name: Korhely Étterem
places.note: Pub-restaurant in the centre: soup, the beef stew and a half-litre of Pécsi lager came to 9,315 forints, about 29 dollars; a 0.3l beer from 1,020. Open daily, to 23:00 on Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Reggeli
places.note: Breakfast café on Király utca, 4.7 from 1,835 reviews: American pancakes and a cold brew for 4,600 forints, about 14 dollars, or the Buddha bowl at 3,300. Daily 08:00 to 15:00.

places.name: Bohemia Sörkonyha
places.note: Czech beer kitchen: chicken soup, the pork knuckle and a half-litre of Lobkowicz came to 9,600 forints, about 30 dollars. Closed Monday and Tuesday, Wednesday dinner only from 17:00, to midnight Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Tihany Abbey
places.note: Founded in 1055; the present church is from 1763, with Lotz ceiling frescoes and King Andrew I's tomb in the crypt. 3,400 forints, about 11 dollars; October hours 10:00 to 17:00 (Sunday from 11:15), November to March to 16:00, and the ticket office shuts 30 minutes early.

places.name: Festetics Palace
places.note: Kristóf Festetics began it in 1745; the library wing of 1799 to 1801 holds about 90,000 volumes, and there is a coach museum. About 17 dollars, daily 10:00 to 18:00; it is 53 km away in a straight line, so it is a full day with the Balaton Museum.

places.name: Balaton Museum
places.note: The lake's own museum, opened in 1928: its history, fishing and an aquarium; about 10 dollars. Closed Sunday and Monday, so put the Keszthely day midweek.

places.name: Lake Hévíz
places.note: A thermal lake you swim in, just past Keszthely. Hours and ticket price were not confirmed; check the price before you drive.

places.name: Lóczy Cave
places.note: A cave in Balatonfüred, seen on hourly guided tours of about 20 minutes, in Hungarian only. Hours and ticket price unknown; check the price.

places.name: Tihany Lavender Field
places.note: The lavender on the Tihany peninsula; it flowers around June and there is nothing to see in April. Price unknown, so check the price if you pick your own.

places.name: Annagora Aquapark
places.note: Waterpark in Balatonfüred: the adult all-in pass online is about 34 dollars, daily 10:00 to 19:00. The wet-weather day.

places.name: Régi Idők Udvara
places.note: An open-air heritage site in Tihany village with a restaurant in it. Closed Tuesdays; admission and menu prices were not found, so check the price.

places.name: Bistro Sparhelt
places.note: Balatonfüred's Michelin Bib Gourmand: soup, main and dessert came to 15,300 forints, about 47 dollars. Closed Monday and Tuesday; it shuts between 17:00 and 18:00, so book either lunch or dinner.

places.name: Halászkert
places.note: The lake-fish house, 4.6 from 4,527 reviews: fish soup, the cheapest fish main and a dessert came to 8,570 forints, about 27 dollars. Pike-perch is priced by weight at 1,490 per 10 dkg, so ask before it lands. Open daily.

places.name: Taverna Étterem és Vendégház
places.note: Guesthouse restaurant, 4.7 from 2,384 reviews: soup, a chicken main and dessert came to 11,170 forints, about 35 dollars. Hours vary, check before walking over.

places.name: Kotyogós Kávéterasz
places.note: Brunch terrace in Tihany, 4.7 on Google: American pancakes and a cappuccino come to 5,180 forints, about 16 dollars. Brunch 08:30 to 16:00; closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Apátsági Rege Cukrászda
places.note: The pastry shop under the abbey, 4.6 from over 10,000 reviews; a slice of cream cake works out about 1,500 forints, 5 dollars. Open daily to 21:00, Saturday 22:00.

places.name: Tihanyi Vinarius
places.note: Wine bar, 4.8 on Google: a 2dl nagyfröccs, wine and soda, is about 3,250 forints, 10 dollars, per the 2026 list. Closed Monday and Tuesday.

places.name: Bodorka Balaton Aquarium
places.note: A compact visitor centre on the lake front that shows the fish and water life of Lake Balaton, including wild fish close up; about 20 minutes is enough, so pair it with a walk along the Tagore promenade. Adult ticket about 6 dollars (Wanderlog lists it in dollars).

places.name: Vaszary Gallery
places.note: Opened in 2010 in a former grand house with an English-style garden; shows János Vaszary, with works by Rodin, Miró and Ilona Keserü, plus a retro Balatonfüred exhibition and a garden coffee spot. Check the price. Closed Monday and Tuesday; most labels are in Hungarian only.

places.name: Jókai Mór Memorial House
places.note: The 1870 villa where Mór Jókai and his actress wife Róza Laborfalvy spent summers from 1870 to 1890, and where he wrote novels including The Golden Man. It keeps his writing furniture, belongings and her stage costumes. Check the price and opening hours, which were not found.

places.name: Barátlakások (hermit caves)
places.note: The cave dwellings of a former monastic community on the Tihany peninsula; some chambers have been destroyed, but the site is explored freely without a guide. Check the price; hours not found.

places.name: Tihanyi Tájházak (local houses)
places.note: Two houses restored in 2018: a farmer's house on farming and a fisherman's house with traditional fishing tools. Adult ticket about 3 dollars (Wanderlog lists it in dollars). Open 10:00 to 16:00 Monday to Friday and Sunday, Saturday to 17:00.

sources: sights-v2 2026-10-27: sights reworked to the SIGHTS standard (Google Maps categories, official pages, Wikipedia)

Reddit was unreachable for all four beds; meals ranked by Michelin Bib Gourmand and Google rating and review counts (via Wanderlog), prices from the venues' own menus at 0.0031 USD per forint (valutafx, 2026-07-24).

destination.name: Hungary: Budapest, Eger, Pécs and Lake Balaton
destination.pitch: Budapest carries the week: Parliament, Castle Hill, a morning in Széchenyi's pools. Give it four nights, then two in Eger for the castle and the wine valley, and two in Pécs or on Balaton.
destination.caveat: Gellért Baths are closed for renovation until 2028 and Király since 2020, so Széchenyi is the bath. Parliament tours sell out weeks ahead at about 72 dollars for non-EU visitors. Pécs and Eger museums close Mondays, and Balaton is a summer lake. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Budapest: ruin bars in District VII, the Chain Bridge at night, the Central Market Hall in the morning, and Andrássy út from the Opera to Heroes' Square.
because.food: Three Bib Gourmands in Budapest (N28, Cabrio, Goli), lángos at Retro Lángos for 11 dollars, pork knuckle in Eger's wine valley and lake fish at Halászkert.
because.culture: Parliament and the National Gallery in Budapest, the 1552 siege at Eger Castle, 4th-century tombs and Zsolnay porcelain in Pécs, the Lotz frescoes in Tihany Abbey.
because.relaxation: Széchenyi's outdoor pools in Budapest, the Ottoman Turkish Bath in Eger, and a slow two days on the Tihany peninsula with cake under the abbey.
because.exploration: Eger's wine valley cellars, the City Under the City tunnels, the communist statues of Memento Park and the Misina tower above Pécs.
